original_value: In recent years, with the rapid development of mobile app ecosystem, the number and categories of mobile apps have grown tremendously. However, the global prevalence of mobile apps also leads to fierce competition. As a result, many apps will disappear. To thrive in this competitive app market, it is vital for app developers to understand the popularity evolution of their mobile apps, and inform strategic decision-making for better mobile app development. Therefore, it is significant and necessary to model and forecast the future popularity evolution of mobile apps. The popularity evolution of mobile apps is usually a long-term process, affected by various complex factors. However, existing works lack the capabilities to model such complex factors. To better understand the popularity evolution, in this paper, we aim to forecast the popularity evolution of mobile apps by incorporating complex factors, i.e., exogenous stimulis and endogenous excitations. Specifically, we propose a model based on the Multivariate Hawkes Process (MHP), which is an exogenous stimulis-driven self-exciting point process, to model the exogenous stimulis and endogenous excitations simultaneously. Extensive experimental studies on a real-world dataset from app store demonstrate that MHP outperforms the state-of-the-art methods regarding popularity evolution forecasting.

result.paraphrase: In recent years, the mobile app ecosystem has developed rapidly, leading to a tremendous increase in both the number and variety of apps. At the same time, their worldwide popularity has intensified competition, causing many apps to disappear. For developers to succeed in this competitive market, it is essential to understand how app popularity evolves and to use that insight to support strategic decisions and improve development. Accordingly, modeling and forecasting the future popularity evolution of mobile apps is both important and necessary. This evolution is typically a long-term process influenced by many complex factors, yet existing methods cannot adequately capture them. To better analyze popularity evolution, this paper aims to forecast mobile app popularity by incorporating complex factors, namely exogenous stimuli and endogenous excitations. Specifically, we propose a model built on the Multivariate Hawkes Process (MHP), an exogenous-stimuli-driven self-exciting point process, to jointly model exogenous stimuli and endogenous excitations. Extensive experiments on a real-world app store dataset show that MHP outperforms state-of-the-art methods in forecasting popularity evolution.
